disease_label_per_paper: Testicular abscess and ischemia secondary to epididymo-orchitis
presentation_summary: 67-year-old man presented to the emergency department with one week of right scrotal pain and swelling.
He initially noticed right scrotal swelling, then pain radiating to the right inguinal region, and also reported chills, fever, nausea, and vomiting.
He denied lower urinary tract symptoms.

Past history included urinary retention due to benign prostatic hypertrophy, intermittent self-catheter dependence for one year, hypertension, and chronic kidney disease; several weeks before presentation he reduced intermittent catheterization to twice daily because spontaneous voiding had increased.
Presentation vitals showed tachycardia 108 beats/minute, temperature 101.7 F, and normal blood pressure.
Genital examination showed a tender indurated right hemiscrotum with thinning superficial skin; the testis was non-palpable because of swelling.
Urinalysis showed leukocyte esterase, WBCs, and bacteria; serum labs showed WBC 21.1 x 10^9/L with 85% neutrophils.

Initial scrotal Doppler ultrasound showed heterogeneous right testis and epididymis, a large markedly complex hydrocele, and preserved arterial and venous flow, suggesting epididymo-orchitis; CT did not demonstrate abscess or additional pathology.

quality_warnings: Urine culture species, wound culture species, operative purulence, orchiectomy, pathology-confirmed abscess/ischemic necrosis, and treatment response are preserved as non-ranking evidence.
Initial imaging showed preserved Doppler flow and did not detect abscess; these presentation facts are retained even though later operative/pathology evidence proved abscess and ischemic necrosis.
Self-catheterization and chronic kidney disease are risk/treatment-context evidence, not disease labels.
